function.description: Replace an exact snippet of an existing file, leaving the rest untouched. This is the tool to use for changing code. `old_string` must reproduce the file's current text byte for byte, including indentation and newlines, and must appear exactly once unless `replace_all` is true - include a few surrounding lines to make it unique. Do not include the `NNN| ` line-number prefixes that read_file adds. To delete code, pass an empty `new_string`.
function.name: edit_file

new_string.description: Text to put in its place. Empty string deletes the snippet.

old_string.description: Exact text to find, copied verbatim from the file.

path.description: Path to the file to edit, absolute or relative to the working directory.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one. Defaults to false.

function.description: Read a text file and return its contents with 1-based line numbers prefixed as `NNN| `. Read a file before editing it so `edit_file` snippets match exactly. Long files come back in pages; when there is more, the output ends with the offset to continue from. The line numbers are display only - never include them in `edit_file` arguments. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files come back as images you can see.
function.name: read_file

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return.

offset.description: 1-based line to start at. Defaults to 1.

path.description: Path to the file, absolute or relative to the working directory.

function.description: Run a shell command and return its combined stdout and stderr, plus the exit code when it is non-zero. Every command starts in the working directory, so there is no need to `cd` into it first. Use it to build, test, run linters, search with `rg`, `grep` or `find`, and explore with `ls`. Read and change files with `read_file`, `edit_file` and `write_file`. The command is non-interactive: it cannot prompt, and it is killed at the timeout. Output is truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50.0KB, whichever is hit first, and then the full output is saved to a temp file.
function.name: run_command

command.description: Shell command, for example `cargo test -p uji`.

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is killed. Defaults to 120.

function.description: Write a file from scratch, creating parent directories as needed. This replaces the entire file, so use it for new files only. To change an existing file use `edit_file` instead - overwriting loses everything you did not include.
function.name: write_file

path.description: Path to write, absolute or relative to the working directory.
